text: 220 controlled mutations across 11 classes were applied to 20 strong contracts, each changing exactly one invariant. The share of classes whose declared primitive moved in the declared direction with an interval excluding zero is 63.6%.

author: claude/hguv

caveats: Mutations are synthetic and author-written; they can themselves bias which primitives move.
Paired movement is measured against the same contract before mutation, so contract-to-contract variation is controlled.
result_summary.decision: Use the mutation table to decide which primitives are trustworthy enough to compose; investigate any class whose declared primitive does not move.
result_summary.plain_language: 220 controlled mutations across 11 classes were applied to 20 strong contracts, each changing exactly one invariant. The share of classes whose declared primitive moved in the declared direction with an interval excluding zero is 63.6%.
supported_claims: Each of the 11 mutation classes changed exactly one declared invariant of a structurally valid, labelled-ready contract.
unsupported_claims: That the battery is complete: mutations test the primitives they name, not readiness in general.
